user_listening_observation: The bass resonates too far into the following subdivision.
The pitch changes while the previous bass tone is still audibly ringing.
If bass sustain is used, the sustained portion should remain the same tone.
rule_under_test: A sustained bass tone may ring only while pitch remains unchanged; any pitch change must begin as a distinct new attack after the previous tone is released.
diagnosis: The source pattern itself contains overlapping attacks with different chord-relative degrees.
This creates simultaneous or tail-overlapping bass pitches before any sustain candidate is applied.
The current Growlybass sample tail makes these source-writing overlaps more audible.
Bass sustain duration tuning cannot repair a pitch-coherence violation already present in the symbolic source.
repair_direction: Preserve the approved downbeat attack timing.
Do not extend a bass note through a later attack of a different pitch.
If a bass tone is intended to sustain across a subdivision, keep the same pitch through that sustain.
Treat any root-to-fifth or fifth-to-root move as a discrete new note with the previous pitch released first.
Do not add a new pitch change merely to create rhythmic movement.
